Body.Content:
What and Why:

Users will soon be able to build richer, end-to-end automations in Workflows for Microsoft Teams by adding multiple actions within a single workflow. Instead of creating and managing separate workflows for individual tasks, users can design automated processes that perform several actions in sequence after a single trigger.

This enhancement provides a more intuitive, step-based workflow building experience and enables users to automate common business scenarios such as collecting information, sending notifications, updating systems, and routing requests within a single workflow.

Rollout Schedule:

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early September 2026 and is expected to complete by early September 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early September 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-September 2026.

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • Users of Workflows for Microsoft Teams.

Platform:

  • Microsoft Teams

With this update, users will be able to:

  • Reduce manual and repetitive work by automating multiple tasks within a single workflow.
  • Consolidate business processes that previously required multiple separate workflows.
  • Improve productivity by automating more complete business scenarios from start to finish.
  • Simplify workflow management and maintenance through a clearer, step-based design experience.
  • Address more complex business needs without requiring advanced technical expertise.

The result is a more flexible and scalable automation experience that helps teams save time and work more efficiently.

Action Required / Recommendations:

No action is required from administrators. This feature will be available automatically to Workflows users once the rollout reaches your organization.

You may want to inform users about this new capability and update any internal guidance or training materials related to creating workflows in Microsoft Teams.

Details.Name: Summary
Details.Value: Microsoft Teams Workflows will soon support multiple sequential actions in a single workflow, enabling richer automations to reduce manual tasks, consolidate processes, and improve productivity. The feature rolls out worldwide in early to mid-September 2026, requiring no admin action but user awareness updates.

Title: Microsoft Teams: Add multiple steps when building a workflow from scratch
